# Analytics & Telemetry
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/analytics</source>

Satisium Starter features a unified telemetry architecture that routes events to PostHog, Google Analytics, and an optional Upstash Redis counter in a single call.

## The Unified `trackEvent` Facade

Import `trackEvent` from `lib/analytics.ts`:

```tsx

export function ExportButton() {
  const handleExport = () => {
    trackEvent("export_artifact", {
      format: "svg",
      elementsCount: 42,
    })
  }

  return <button onClick={handleExport}>Export SVG</button>
}
```

### What Happens Behind the Scenes:

1. **Cookie Consent Check:** If the visitor has not accepted cookies, the event is silently ignored or logged in dev mode.
2. **PostHog:** Automatically dispatches via `posthog.capture(eventName, properties)`.
3. **Google Analytics:** Automatically dispatches via `window.gtag("event", eventName, properties)`.
4. **Public Counter (Optional):** If the third argument is passed (e.g. `trackEvent(..., ..., "page_view")`), it calls `/api/telemetry` to increment a rate-limited Redis metric.

---

## Activating Analytics Providers

The starter operates under the **zero-key rule**: if no keys are provided, analytics silently degrade to no-ops without throwing errors.

To activate analytics in production, add keys to `.env.local`:

```bash
# PostHog Product Analytics
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN="phc_your_token_here"
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST="https://us.i.posthog.com"

# Google Analytics (GA4)
NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID="G-XXXXXXXXXX"

# Upstash Redis Telemetry Counter (Optional)
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL="https://...upstash.io"
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN="..."
```

---

## Core Web Vitals (CWV)

The template automatically streams Core Web Vitals (`LCP`, `INP`, `CLS`, `FID`, `TTFB`) from `next/web-vitals` to your PostHog analytics dashboard whenever consent is granted.

---

# Project Configuration
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/configuration</source>

Satisium Starter centralizes configuration so you never have to search across dozens of files to update branding.

## 1. Single Source of Truth (`config/site.ts`)

All product branding, author information, repository URLs, social handles, and legal notices live in `config/site.ts`:

```ts
export const PRODUCT = {
  name: "My Tool",
  shortName: "Tool",
  titleTemplate: "%s | My Tool",
  defaultTitle: "My Tool — High-Performance SVG Editor",
  description: "An intuitive in-browser tool built on Satisium.",
} as const
```

- **`PRODUCT`:** Controls default HTML title tags, meta descriptions, and OpenGraph labels.
- **`PROJECT`:** Controls official project social links (X/Twitter, GitHub, Discord, Instagram).
- **`AUTHOR`:** Controls the creator profile and attribution.
- **`LEGAL`:** Controls the updated date and legal footer parameters.

---

## 2. Brand Tokens & Design System (`app/globals.css`)

Depth in Satisium is established purely through **OKLCH luminance tokens**, avoiding artificial drop shadows:

- `bg-background` — Base surface (lightest in light mode, darkest in dark mode).
- `bg-card` — Primary container cards and structural panels.
- `bg-muted` — Secondary recessed surfaces and controls.
- `text-foreground` — High-contrast body typography.
- `text-muted-foreground` — Low-contrast supporting metadata and captions.

<Callout type="warning">
  <strong>Zero Opacity Modifiers:</strong> Never write Tailwind opacity
  modifiers like <code>bg-primary/20</code> or{" "}
  <code>text-muted-foreground/80</code>. Use semantic surface tokens directly.
</Callout>

---

## 3. Brand Assets Checklist

After running `pnpm setup`, replace these four files to complete your visual identity:

1. **Favicon & Mobile Bookmark:** Replace `app/icon.svg`, `app/apple-icon.png`, and `app/favicon.ico`.
2. **Social Card Background:** Replace `public/og-bg-optimized.jpg` (1200×630px).
3. **Logo Mark:** Replace `public/satisium.png` (512×512px).
4. **Brand Font (Optional):** Replace `public/nulshock.bold.otf` if your product uses a distinct headline typeface.

---

# Installation & Quickstart
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/installation</source>

<PromptBlock
  title="Agent Prompt"
  prompt="Read PRODUCTION_READINESS_PLAN.md, run pnpm setup, and initialize the project."
/>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Clone and install dependencies">
    Clone the template repository into your new product directory:

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/satisium/starter.git my-product
    cd my-product
    pnpm install
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure your product with pnpm setup">
    Run the interactive Satisium product scaffolder:

    ```bash
    pnpm setup
    ```

    The CLI will ask for:
    1. **Product Name** (e.g. `Tweak`)
    2. **Production Domain** (e.g. `https://tweak.satisium.com`)
    3. **Preset Choice**:
       * `tool` — Interactive workstation canvas + product docs
       * `ui` — Component library + Shadcn registry + live previewer

    <Callout type="info">
      Non-interactive mode for CI or scripts:
      <code>pnpm setup --name "Tweak" --slug tweak --domain https://tweak.satisium.com --preset tool</code>
    </Callout>

  </Step>

  <Step title="Start the development server">
    Launch the Next.js Turbopack development server:

    ```bash
    pnpm dev
    ```

    * Visit [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) for your curated landing page.
    * Visit `/app` for your product workstation canvas.
    * Visit `/docs` for your Fumadocs documentation engine.

  </Step>
</Steps>

## The Zero-Key Rule

The Satisium Starter adheres to a strict **zero-key rule**: every environment variable in `.env.example` is optional.
A fresh clone with an empty `.env.local` will boot, build, and pass all tests out-of-the-box. When you are ready to configure analytics or telemetry, add keys to `.env.local`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

## Architectural Health Check

Verify your setup at any time with the 13-point Satisium architectural auditor:

```bash
pnpm check:doctor
```

---

# Product Presets (UI vs Tool)
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/presets</source>

Satisium Starter standardizes on two production presets: **`tool`** and **`ui`**.

## The Two Presets at a Glance

| Feature                            | `tool` Preset                                                    | `ui` Preset                                                |
| :--------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Primary Target**                 | Interactive tools, editors, SaaS utilities (e.g. Tweak, Typeset) | Component libraries, design systems (e.g. Satisium Pro UI) |
| **Product Workstation (`/app`)**   | Clean, blank canvas ready for your application logic             | Minimal entrypoint                                         |
| **Documentation Engine (`/docs`)** | User guides, onboarding, hotkeys reference                       | Component reference docs with interactive previewers       |
| **Shadcn Open Registry**           | Pruned (`public/r/*.json` removed)                               | Active (`public/r/*.json` compiled via Shadcn standard)    |
| **Component Previewer**            | Pruned (`components/previewer` removed)                          | Active (Live resizable previewer & embed routes)           |
| **Marketing Landing Page**         | High-conversion product landing + "Open App" CTA                 | Component library showcase + "Copy CLI" install commands   |

---

## Preset 1: `tool` (Interactive Tools & Apps)

Choose the `tool` preset when building interactive web utilities, creative tools, or SaaS workstation apps:

```bash
pnpm setup --name "Tweak" --slug tweak --domain https://tweak.app --preset tool
```

### What Happens During Setup:

1. Prunes `registry/`, `public/r/`, `app/preview/`, `app/embed/`, and `components/previewer/`.
2. Updates `components/docs/doc-demo-renderer.tsx` to a no-op adapter so documentation builds with zero TypeScript errors.
3. Automatically cleans up `lib/nav.ts` to remove the "Components" navigation link from the site header, rail, and ⌘K palette.
4. Leaves `app/app/page.tsx` as a clean, blank slate ready for your canvas and controls.

---

## Preset 2: `ui` (Component Library & Registry)

Choose the `ui` preset when building a distributable design system or component kit:

```bash
pnpm setup --name "Satisium Pro UI" --slug satisium-pro-ui --domain https://ui.satisium.com --preset ui
```

### What Happens During Setup:

1. Retains the full Shadcn Open Registry pipeline.
2. Keeps the live component previewer, embed endpoints (`/embed/[registryKey]`), and fullscreen preview routes.
3. Configures `registry.json` with your product homepage and distribution URLs.
4. Distribute components to external projects via:
   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.satisium.com/r/action-button.json
   ```

---

# Project Structure
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/project-structure</source>

The template is organized into clear architectural layers adhering to strict placement conventions:

<FileTree
  files={{
    "app/layout.tsx": "Root shell, fonts, and metadata",
    "app/page.tsx": "Landing page and marketing hero",
    "app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx": "Fumadocs documentation engine",
    "app/docs/[[...slug]]/layout.tsx":
      "Resolves the page, picks the docs shell",
    "app/app/page.tsx": "Application workspace",
    "components/docs/types.ts": "The docs layout contract",
    "components/docs/dispatch.tsx":
      "Chooses the docs shell from NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_LAYOUT",
    "components/docs/shell.tsx": "DocsScreen + DocsPane (borderless shell)",
    "components/docs/layouts/three-pane.tsx":
      "Borderless three-pane docs layout",
    "components/docs/layouts/spatial.tsx": "Signature card-shift docs layout",
    "components/ui/button.tsx": "Button primitive",
    "components/ui/empty-state.tsx": "Reusable empty state",
    "components/ui/loading-state.tsx": "Skeleton & spinner",
    "components/mdx/file-tree.tsx": "MDX file tree component",
    "components/mdx/steps.tsx": "Numbered walkthrough steps",
    "content/docs": "Markdown & MDX documentation",
    "lib/routes.ts": "Typed route registry",
    "lib/config.ts": "Brand and site configuration",
    "lib/nav.ts": "Navigation architecture",
  }}
/>

## Directory Overview

- **`app/`**: Next.js App Router surfaces — landing, docs engine, app workspace, API routes.
- **`components/ui/`**: Reusable atomic primitives adhering to Satisium tokens.
- **`components/mdx/`**: MDX-exclusive documentation components (`Steps`, `PromptBlock`, `FileTree`).
- **`content/docs/`**: Markdown source pages rendered by Fumadocs.
- **`lib/`**: Framework-free utilities, route constants, typed navigation, and telemetry.

---

# SEO, OpenGraph & AI Discovery (AEO)
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/getting-started/seo-and-aeo</source>

Satisium Starter ensures that every page is fully indexable by traditional search engines (Google, Bing) and discoverable by modern AI engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity).

## 1. Dynamic Social Cards (`/api/og`)

Every route automatically generates a 1200×630px social preview card for Twitter/X, Discord, and LinkedIn:

- **Endpoint:** `/api/og?title=<Title>&label=<Category>`
- Rendered on the Node.js runtime using `next/og` and `@vercel/og`.
- Rendered using `PlusJakartaSans-Bold.ttf` over `public/og-bg-optimized.jpg`.
- You can test your card in development:
  ```text
  http://localhost:3000/api/og?title=My+Tool&label=WORKSTATION
  ```

---

## 2. Setting Page Metadata

Use the typed `buildMetadata()` helper from `lib/metadata.ts` on any new route:

```tsx

export const metadata = buildMetadata({
  title: "Tool Canvas",
  description: "High-performance vector tool canvas.",
  path: ROUTES.app,
})
```

This automatically generates canonical links, OpenGraph image tags, Twitter Summary Large Image cards, and language alternates.

---

## 3. AEO (AI Engine Optimization & LLMs)

Autonomous AI agents (Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor) explore web documentation differently than human visitors. Satisium generates a machine-readable knowledge base before every production build:

- **`public/llms.txt`:** The structured index file AI agents look for first.
- **`public/llms-full.txt`:** Concatenated raw markdown knowledge base for 1-shot context injection.
- **`public/llms/*.md`:** Clean markdown files corresponding to each documentation route.

### Testing the LLM Pipeline:

```bash
pnpm llm
```

### Search Crawlers & AI Robots (`app/robots.ts`):

Satisium explicitly configures permissions for AI indexing bots (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`), allowing them priority access to your `/llms.txt` knowledge base while protecting private embed routes.

---

# Overview
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs</source>

**Ease** is an interactive cubic-bezier editor and spring physics studio designed for modern design engineers. Craft, inspect, and fine-tune fluid motion curves and mathematical spring dynamics, then export production-ready code directly into CSS, Tailwind CSS, Motion, and GSAP.

## Core Capabilities

- **Interactive Cubic-Bezier Editor:** Drag control handles with sub-pixel precision and real-time bounding box adjustments.
- **Analytical Spring Physics Solver:** Tune physical mass, stiffness, damping, and initial velocity with instant numerical integration.
- **Multi-Property Live Preview:** Test your curves simultaneously across translation, scale, opacity, and rotation in an interactive stage.
- **Universal Code Export:** One-click copy formatted for native CSS `cubic-bezier()`, modern CSS `linear()` spring approximations, Tailwind CSS v4 keyframe configs, Motion spring transitions, and GSAP `CustomEase`.

## The Studio Architecture

The Ease studio is located at [`/app`](/app). It features a 3-column workstation:

1. **Left Rail:** Catalog of standardized cubic-bezier presets and calibrated physical springs.
2. **Center Canvas:** Real-time graph visualizer with dynamic auto-zoom and multi-property animation preview stage.
3. **Right Rail:** Curve behavioral characteristics, recommended use-cases, and multi-target code generation.

---

# Curve Presets
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/presets</source>

Ease provides curated animation curves calibrated for common user interface states.

## Standard Beziers

- **Swift In-Out:** `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0)` — Standard acceleration and deceleration for modals, drawers, and page transitions.
- **Snappy Out:** `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1.0, 0.3, 1.0)` — Fast initial entry with gentle deceleration for dropdowns and tooltips.
- **Emphasized:** `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` — Dramatic material curve for primary navigational elements.

## Calibrated Springs

- **Bouncy:** High stiffness with underdamped oscillation for playful interactions and celebration toasts.
- **Gentle:** Moderately damped curve with minimal overshoot for fluid sheet reveals and subtle focus rings.
- **Wobbly:** Multi-cycle oscillation ideal for attention-seeking indicators and micro-feedback badges.

---

# Spring Physics
<source>https://ease.satisium.com/docs/springs</source>

Unlike static duration-based cubic-beziers, springs simulate actual physical forces. A spring does not have an arbitrary duration; its motion duration is an emergent property derived from physical dynamics.

## Physical Parameters

| Parameter     | Symbol | Range       | Description                                                                                |
| :------------ | :----- | :---------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Mass**      | $m$    | `0.1 – 5.0` | The inertia of the moving object. Higher mass creates heavier, more sluggish motion.       |
| **Stiffness** | $k$    | `1 – 500`   | The tension of the spring. Higher stiffness causes faster, snappier oscillations.          |
| **Damping**   | $c$    | `1 – 100`   | The friction resisting the motion. High damping suppresses oscillation (critical damping). |

## CSS `linear()` Approximations

Traditional CSS transitions cannot compute spring physics natively. Ease bridges this gap by solving the harmonic differential equation and sampling the motion into a modern CSS `linear()` function:

```css
.ease-spring {
  transition: transform 1.2s
    linear(
      0,
      0.009,
      0.035,
      0.078,
      0.136,
      0.207,
      0.289,
      0.38,
      0.477,
      0.578,
      0.679,
      0.778,

      1.135,
```
